title: Cooldown window spectroscopy - nanopulse correlation scratchpad
content:
Goal: quickly capture anomaly where short high-qps nanopulse arrivals (50-200ms wide) correlate with transient GPU temperature spikes and a 5–15ms tail on p99. Hypothesis: a short cooldown window after a microburst triggers power/clock gating behavior on the GPU or kernel fallback that increases serialization for KV-cache updates, amplifying tail latency.

Experiment(s) run (quick list):
1) pulseA: 1s baseline @ 20 qps, 200ms nanopulse @ 500 qps (sine-ish), 1s recovery, repeat 120s.
2) pulseB-cool: same as A but insert forced cool (pause dcache warm prefill) 300ms after burst.
3) pulseC-quant: A with int8 quant on model + reduced batch size.
4) control: steady 60 qps for 5m.

Environment:
- Model: llama-ish-13b-v2 (production-compat stub)
- Nodes: p4d-equivalent (8xA100-sim) dedicated test pool
- Runtime: rti-3.2 (kv-cache on), binary build: 2024-12-19
- Tracing: per-request token traces, kernel-power csv from nvidia-smi poll @100ms
- Warm cache: prefilled with 32 context entries before pulses

What I measured:
- per-request latency (p50/p95/p99)
- token throughput curve across the burst window
- GPU temp and power (100ms samples)
- batch sizes observed, concurrency, queue depth

Representative raw excerpt (times are relative, ms):
[time, qps, p50, p95, p99, gpu_temp, batches]
0.0, 25, 8.3, 12.1, 14.5, 62, 1
200.0, 500, 9.0, 18.2, 34.6, 72, 5
350.0, 120, 7.9, 11.8, 13.6, 74, 2
520.0, 30, 8.1, 12.0, 13.0, 68, 1

Quick ascii timeline (latency p99) relative 0..700ms:
0ms  [======] 14ms
200ms[===============] 34ms (spike)
350ms[===] 13ms
520ms[==] 13ms

Observations: 
- PulseA: p99 spikes align ~80–160ms after the leading edge of the burst and map to a ~6–12 W jump in GPU power, temp rises 8–12C inside ~300ms.
- PulseB-cool: inserting the small cooldown reduces p99 by ~6ms but increases p95 slightly; suggests some requests are being serialized by cooldown gating while others avoid hot-path contention.
- PulseC-quant: quantization reduces overall p50/p95 but p99 spike amplitude stays similar — implies tail is system-level not model compute-bound.
- Control: no p99 structure beyond expected jitter.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) GPU power/clock gating: short bursts push a core power regime change that causes brief kernel scheduling jitter (locks/driver hysteresis).
2) Runtime KV-cache writeback: bursts + eviction cause a short period of synchronous eviction/compaction that blocks fast-path token generation.
3) OS-level CPU interrupt burst (nv-host engine stalls) that delays completion callbacks, backpressureing runtime.

Quick checks to validate:
- correlate kernel launch latency from trace with p99 peaks (add step to capture cudaEvent timings).
- run same pulse with NVML telemetry at 10ms to see microsecond structure.
- change runtime to async writeback mode (if available) to test KV hypothesis.
- inject synthetic GPU clock lock (nvidia-smi -ac) to see effect.

Notes / side-effects seen:
- When cooldown inserted, we see a small bin of requests that jump to higher latency (outliers) while majority smooths — suggests bimodal behavior.
- Some runs show that increasing batch size cap from 8->12 mutes the p99 but shifts p95 worse, classic trade-off.

Immediate next steps (short):
- 1) Add cudaEvent markers in the runtime around KV writeback + kernel launch (Kenny/Liam).
- 2) Re-run pulseA with NVML @ 10ms sampling (Maya).
- 3) Try async-writeback branch (eng-try/async-wb) on a 3-node test pool.
- 4) Create a small dashboard with a waterfall view: p99 vs kernel-latency vs GPU-power (low effort) — use grafana panel from mr/214.

Longer-term ideas:
- Explore a "cooldown-aware" admission controller that smooths the last few requests after a nanopulse to avoid kernel mode changes.
- Runtime knob: defer KV-eviction until queue depth below X or do background compaction with priority lane.

Open questions I still have: 
- Is the temp jump cause or effect? Could a driver-level freq change causing more heat be the real trigger?
- Are specific kernels (attention/cross-attention) consistently the ones that delay? Need symbol-level trace.

To-do (tabled):
- [ ] Add kernel-level timings to tracing pipeline
- [ ] Confirm async writeback branch boots on p4d tests
- [ ] Reproduce on smaller A10 machines (cost check)
- [ ] File JIRA with initial evidence and assign to runtime infra

Slack thread: #eng-runtime / "nanopulse-cooldown". Quick ping to Maya and Liam noting results (01/12).

Random miscellany/future notes:
- If we see same pattern across quantized and fp16, that strengthens the system-level thesis.
- Could be worth a short experiment running host-level stress (cpu irq churn) to reproduce p99 pattern without GPU heating; if reproduced, that implies OS/driver path.

Signed-off scratch log: Sana Iyer, experimental notes saved; will attach traces to Jira-ENG-1985 after kernel-timing run.
